# Product review

Read the actual plan and relevant project evidence. Check the promised user outcome, the narrowest useful scope, alternatives including doing nothing, adoption friction, and whether the proposed work solves the stated problem. Separate a demonstrated defect from a product hypothesis. Explain tradeoffs concretely and identify the few decisions that could materially change the result.

Keep user-approved scope intact. A new idea, adjacent cleanup, or outside opinion is a finding, not authorization to expand. Amend the same plan only within authorized scope. Record changed assumptions and unresolved decisions, then return to the parent plan flow.
